LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.1: Whole Numbers

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Whole Numbers. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use place value and total value of digits up to tens of thousands in daily life situations
2. read and write numbers up to 10,000 in symbols in real-life situations
3. read and write numbers up to 1,000 in words in day-to-day activities
4. order numbers up to 1,000 in different situations
5. identify factors of numbers upto 50 in different contexts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WHOLE NUMBERS
Whole Numbers is a Grade mathematics skill used at school, at the market, and at home.

HOW TO STUDY THIS TOPIC
1. Read each idea slowly.
2. Copy every worked example into your book and recalculate it yourself.
3. Then try the practice questions without looking at the answers.

WORKED EXAMPLE STYLE
Write the question clearly. Show each step. Box the final answer.
Example framework:
  Question: (write a Whole Numbers problem)
  Step 1: …
  Step 2: …
  Answer: …

KENYAN CONTEXT
Use shillings, market goods, school desks, or garden plots as story numbers so the maths feels real.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Solve one simple Whole Numbers question using objects or a drawing.

Example 2: Solve a harder Whole Numbers question showing every step.

Example 3: Make a word problem about Whole Numbers set at a Kenyan market.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Whole Numbers.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Whole Numbers in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. use place value and total value of digits up to tens of thousands in daily life situations
2. read and write numbers up to 10,000 in symbols in real-life situations
3. read and write numbers up to 1,000 in words in day-to-day activities
4. order numbers up to 1,000 in different situations

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
